identity.title: Obscured star formation in bright z ≃ 7 Lyman-break galaxies
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array observations of the rest-frame far-infrared (FIR) dust continuum emission of six bright Lyman-break galaxies (LBGs) at $z \simeq 7$.

method.value: Stack at UltraVISTA Ks centroids, all six and excluding ID65666

evidence.quote: We produced two stacks, one with all six galaxies included, and one where our detected galaxy ID65666 was excluded.

validation.value: Two stacking methods for IRX consistent to 0.01 dex

evidence.quote: The results of these two methods were consistent to within $\Delta {\rm log}({\rm IRX}) = 0.01$

method.value: Modified blackbody with 1.3 mm flux, CMB correction, integrated 8-1000 um

evidence.quote: The total luminosity was calculated by integrating under the FIR SED from $8\,\mu$m to $1000\,\mu$m.
A dust temperature of $T = 40\,$K was taken as our fiducial value.

assumptions.value: optically thin; CMB contrast correction following DaCunha2013

evidence.quote: We account for the reduced contrast due to the higher temperature of the Cosmic Microwave Background

analysis_steps.goal: SED fitting for photo-z and stellar mass

method.value: LePhare with BC03 models, exponentially declining SFH, Chabrier IMF, 1/5 Zsun, Calzetti dust, 16 bands

evidence.quote: We fitted (cite: Bruzual2003) models assuming an exponentially declining star-formation history (SFH), a (cite: Chabrier2003) initial-mass function, and a metallicity of $1/5\,{\rm Z}_{\odot}$.

validation.value: No acceptable fit at z<6.5 with low-z contaminant templates

evidence.quote: none of the galaxies show an acceptable fit at $z < 6.5$, demonstrating the robustness of the high-redshift solution

analysis_steps.goal: Measure UV slope beta and IRX

method.value: Power-law fit to photometry at 1270-2580 A; Y band excluded for three highest-z galaxies; IRX = L_FIR/L_UV

evidence.quote: The rest-frame UV slope was measured by fitting a power law to the photometry between $\lambda_{\rm rest} = 1270$–$2580$Å (cite: Calzetti1994).

validation.value: Injection-recovery simulations show no significant bias in beta

evidence.quote: We find no significant bias in the recovery of the rest-frame UV slope from the UltraVISTA data

validation.value: Serendipitous sources C1, C2 show no systematic offset

evidence.quote: We therefore find no evidence for any significant systematic astrometric offset between the ALMA data and near-infrared data

results_numeric.quantity: Obscured fraction of SFR in ID65666

evidence.quote: with $75$% of the total SFR being obscured (increasing to $85$% in the case of T$\,= 50\,$K)

findings_qualitative.value: No extremely low IRX at z>5 in this bright sample; results consistent with a Calzetti-like attenuation law.

evidence.quote: Instead, our results are consistent with the predictions of the Calzetti-like dust attenuation law found for star-forming galaxies at lower redshifts.

claims.hypothesis: Bright z~7 LBGs show very low IRX as claimed by earlier z>5 studies
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 imaging and stacking of six LBGs compared with IRX-beta
claims.result: Stack log IRX = -0.08, higher than previous z>5 values
claims.finding: Results consistent with Calzetti-like attenuation, not extremely low IRX

evidence.quote: we find no compelling evidence for extremely low IRX values at $z > 5$

claims.hypothesis: Dust is significant in bright z~7 LBGs
claims.experiment: Stacked FIR luminosity converted to SFR and A_UV
claims.result: SFR_FIR ~30 Msun/yr comparable to UV SFR; A_UV ~0.5-1 mag
claims.finding: Dust obscuration is important in shaping the bright end of the UV LF

evidence.quote: Clearly therefore, dust obscured star-formation is significant in bright $z \simeq 7$ LBGs.

claims.hypothesis: The dust and UV emission in ID65666 are physically offset
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA and HST centroids and test astrometry with serendipitous sources
claims.finding: Inhomogeneous dust distribution with a UV-dark obscured component

evidence.quote: The detection of a serendipitous source in the same ALMA pointing rules out any significant astrometric systematic.

why_this_data.value: Brightest LBGs predicted to be dustiest and can be studied with modest telescope time

evidence.quote: 1) predicted to be the dustiest galaxies from the colour-magnitude relation and 2) can be studied in detail with modest telescope time.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Astrometric systematics as the cause of the offset were rejected using serendipitous sources

evidence.quote: The physical nature of this offset is strengthened by the presence of a bright ALMA source in the same primary beam as ID65666

limitations_admitted.value: L_FIR depends on assumed dust temperature and SED from a single 1.3 mm point; beta errors are large

evidence.quote: requires the assumption of a spectral-energy distribution in the FIR

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-band continuum so L_FIR is dominated by assumed T and beta
Only one detection with 5.2 sigma; stacks are marginal (2.9-4 sigma)
Beta measured from ground-based photometry may be biased by clumpy morphology
